accounts_incomplete_explanation: A half-created account looks functional: the person signs in and receives nothing, or receives without being able to sign in. Creation is resumable.
accounts_broken_promise_explanation: A mail server cannot expire an alias: the purge has not run, and those addresses you believe closed stay open.

match.countPlural=one: This link will let {count} person in.
match.countPlural=*: This link will let {count} people in.

accounts_link_leak_explanation: If it leaks, that is as many accounts created. One link per person costs more to pass on, and far less to revoke.
accounts_admin_role_explanation: The person will be able to grant roles and destroy data.
action_action_could_not_be_started: The action could not be started
action_preview_nothing_changed_yet: Preview — nothing has been changed yet
action_what_will_be_done_in_order: What will be done, in this order:
action_confirmation_explanation: Applying will explicitly confirm "{target}". The role is not enough: repeating the name is what stops you destroying the wrong target.
action_passkey_needed: This takes your passkey. A PocketID window opens; the action is sent once you have presented it.
action_passkey_waiting: Waiting for your passkey… (opening the window again is fine)
action_passkey_blocked: The browser blocked the PocketID window: allow pop-ups for this page, then try again.
action_passkey_timeout: No passkey came back in time: present it again.
action_link_shown_once_explanation: Shown once only: it is recorded nowhere. The QR can also be photographed over your shoulder — do not display it in front of someone it is not meant for.

match.rulesPlural=one: {rules} rule can no longer be evaluated.
match.rulesPlural=*: {rules} rules can no longer be evaluated.

alerts_blind_monitoring_explanation: This is NOT "all is well": collection has probably gone down, and this monitoring has been blind since.
announcements_body_hint: What people need to know, in a few lines.
announcements_incident_visible_to_everyo: This incident will be visible to everyone.
announcements_incident_visible_explanati: It will stay displayed until you close it: an outage that vanishes from the screen on its own makes people believe it is fixed.
announcements_maintenance_reaches_portal: This maintenance will reach the portal.
announcements_maintenance_explanation: The people who only have a mailbox will see it too. Too many operational messages make them stop reading the announcements.
announcements_title_and_body_needed: a title and a body are needed
announcements_update_hint: Where do things stand? This update is added to the thread, it replaces nothing.
announcements_to_close_incident: To close the incident, publish the last update then remove it.
app_assertions_explanation: Read from the running application every night. To read them now:
app_jobs_explanation: Run by the controller in the application's own container when due. To run one now:
app_job_never_run: never run yet — due at once
app_detail_env_explanation: The tokens are shown as they are: their value never leaves the vault, and a visible token says what the app is wired to — which asterisks would not.
app_detail_manifest_frozen_explanation: The installation's, not the current catalog's: it is what is actually running.
app_detail_if_i_lose_everything_now: If I lose everything right now
app_detail_no_backup_recorded: No backup recorded for this application.
app_detail_no_action_recorded: No action recorded on this application.
app_detail_no_manifest_history: No manifest history: the Git mirror is not enabled, and the state only keeps the current version.
app_detail_first_known_version: First known version: there is nothing before it.
app_detail_nothing_to_configure: This application declares no capability, no volume and no environment variable: there is nothing to configure.

match.countPlural=one: {count} application is left with a single copy.
match.countPlural=*: {count} applications are left with a single copy.

backups_at_least_two_copies: Every application has at least two copies.
backups_protection_explanation: The number of declared destinations says nothing about the number of copies: a failing destination protects nothing.
catalog_catalog_unreadable: No application readable. The controller was started without --catalog, or the directory cannot be read.
drift_no_gap: No gap: what is running matches what was decided.
drift_will_be_corrected: Will be corrected on the next pass
drift_correctable_explanation: The Swarm instruction comes from a decision: it gets corrected. These call for no action from you.
drift_refusal_explanation: A system that over-corrects is more dangerous than one that corrects nothing. Here is what Homelabus saw and did not touch, and why.
journal_integrity_explanation: Append-only and chained: each entry carries the previous one's fingerprint. Check the integrity: hlb audit --verify
my_account_service_token_explanation: This access is a service token: it carries a role, not an identity. There is no account behind it, so nothing here is yours.
my_account_no_mailbox: No mailbox. You can sign in, and your address receives nothing — that usually shows on the first lost password reset.
my_account_can_operate: Operate the fleet (scale, back up, restart)
my_account_identity_explanation: Your names, as PocketID gives them to every application you sign in to.
my_account_identity_not_configured: PocketID is not configured on this installation: your names cannot be changed from here.
my_account_identity_not_linked: Your account has no PocketID identity yet. An administrator can finish creating it.
my_account_identity_unreachable: PocketID is not answering: your names cannot be read right now.
my_account_passkeys_explanation: Your passkeys are kept by PocketID alone: you add and remove them there.
my_account_default_mailbox_explanation: Your identity, and the address applications receive from PocketID.
my_account_sessions_explanation: Every browser signed in to this console as you.
my_mailbox_no_mailbox_on_account: No mailbox on this account yet. An alias needs somewhere to deliver.
my_mailbox_local_part_explanation: The part before the @ — the domain is added automatically.
my_mailbox_hint_explanation: Name the recipient, not the address: a random suffix is added. "amazon" alone would be guessable, and a bulk sender tries the obvious ones for the price of one.
my_mailbox_purge_explanation: The purge has not removed them from the mail server. They keep taking mail, and nothing on the sender's side says otherwise.
my_mailbox_no_alias_yet: No alias yet. One address per recipient is what tells you who leaked it.
node_detail_unknown_to_swarm: Swarm does not know this machine: an agent reports it, and no node in the cluster carries its hostname. There is nothing to drain here.
node_detail_protection_a: Verified boot, the disk bound to the network: a signed kernel, the disk opened by the TPM at that kernel's measurements, in its initrd only, and by a Tang of the house.
node_detail_protection_b: The disk bound to the network, the boot not verified: the TPM and a Tang of the house both open it; whoever has the machine inside the house gets a root shell from the boot menu.
node_detail_protection_c: The disk encrypted, the boot chain open: no TPM to bind it to — a Tang, a FIDO2 key or a passphrase opens it, and /boot can be changed unseen.
node_detail_protection_d: Encrypted at rest, the host trusted: a virtual machine, whose host reads its memory and its virtual TPM.
node_detail_protection_ceiling: Detected, never declared — and a ceiling: what the machine can reach, not whether its disk is encrypted yet. After a firmware, TPM or system change, read it again:
node_detail_protection_never_read: Never read on this machine, or Swarm does not know it. Read it:
node_detail_active_explanation: This node takes its share of the work, and Swarm places new containers on it.
node_detail_draining_explanation: Swarm has moved its containers elsewhere and places nothing new here. The machine stays in the cluster.
node_detail_paused_explanation: It keeps what it already runs and takes nothing new.
node_detail_unknown_explanation: Swarm did not say what state this node is in.
node_detail_drain_consequence: Moves every container off this machine and places nothing new on it. What runs elsewhere is untouched, and the node stays in the cluster.
node_detail_return_consequence: Swarm places containers here again. Nothing moves back on its own: what left stays where it went until it is restarted.
node_detail_unreachable_no_measurement: This machine is not answering: there is nothing to measure. What was last known about it is above.
nodes_no_agent_reporting: No agent is reporting. Is the agent service deployed?
plans_no_prepared_plan: No prepared plan. Preview an action, then file it under a name to execute it later.
plans_replay_explanation: Each plan is filed exactly as it was previewed. Replaying it reruns its preview — not the execution: what it describes may have changed since.
plans_no_route: No route takes this plan any more: it is kept, and cannot be replayed.
portal_access_explanation: These applications exist and are exposed. Homelabus does not decide your access rights: your identity carries them.
portal_no_updates_since_published: No updates since it was published.
secrets_without_value_explanation: The values never leave the vault, not even to this page: the API's type has no field to carry them. To read one, you need the master key and the command line.
secrets_rotation_explanation: Rotating a secret is not a write, it is an ordered procedure. The vault is not authoritative: the password ALSO lives in PostgreSQL, at PocketID or at Garage.
secrets_kind_not_recognised: Kind not recognised: no procedure is proposed, it would be invented.
security_exposure_explanation: What each application asks for, against what was really published at the last application of the ingress configuration.

match.countPlural=one: {count} divergence between what is declared and what answers.
match.countPlural=*: {count} divergences between what is declared and what answers.

security_divergence_explanation: An app published by mistake shows nowhere else: not in the manifest, which says the opposite, nor in the list of apps.
security_runbook_explanation: Generated from the real state at the moment you ask for it: inventory of the nodes, destinations, restart order and recovery procedure. Written by hand, a runbook is wrong on the day you need it.
security_runbook_storage_reminder: To be printed and stored OUTSIDE the cluster: a runbook that does not survive the outage it documents documents nothing.
security_break_glass_explanation: Homelabus can verify only the last point itself. The other three are declarations: it keeps the date, and asks again when it ages.
security_verified_by_homelabus: Verified by Homelabus: the trace of a successful drill is what counts, and nothing else.
settings_theme_follows_you: This choice follows you across all your devices: it is stored on the server, not in this browser.
settings_language_explanation: Applies everywhere, immediately — the same choice as the theme. Kept on this device only: unlike the theme, it does not follow you to another browser.
settings_appearance_explanation: The brand and the theme live on the server: changing them does not require recompiling the interface, and they follow across all devices.
settings_legibility_explanation: A theme is not allowed to make the states, the accent or "info" indistinguishable. Every palette is validated: text contrast, and the distinction of every pair under three colour-vision deficiencies — protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia.
signup_no_invitation_explanation: Sign-up happens through a link received from an administrator. If you have one, open it as it is — without retyping part of the address.
signup_name_explanation: This name will be your sign-in identifier AND the local part of your mail address. It cannot be changed afterwards.
signup_name_rules: Lowercase, digits, dot and dash. No space, no capital, no accent.
signup_finish_now_explanation: This link is shown only once and expires in 12 hours. There is no password: your device becomes the key.
signup_incomplete_explanation: Your account exists, but not everything is in place. Report it to the person who invited you: a re-run on their side will finish what is missing.
status_public_warning: This page is PUBLIC: it shows your exposed services and your open incidents to anyone who knows the address.
storage_wizard_explanation: Assembles the command for you — it changes nothing itself. Copy it, then run it yourself on the storage node.
storage_wizard_pool_hint: leave empty if this machine has only one
storage_wizard_import_step: 1. Import the pool, create the datasets
storage_wizard_import_explanation: Importing is reversible (zpool export). Creating a pool is NOT, and this never does it: that command is printed with the disks left to you.
storage_wizard_export_explanation: Printed, not written: the file may already have lines you added, and rewriting it wholesale would drop them.
storage_wizard_value_has_a_space: A space here splits the command below into two arguments, and it will not run.
timeline_nothing_recorded_yet: Nothing recorded yet: no backup, no action.
timeline_river_explanation: Backups and actions in a single dated river. This is where an outage comes close to what preceded it.
todo_ack_is_an_attestation: Marking an action "done" is an attestation, not a checkbox. Ticking it without having done it unblocks a deployment that will fail later, with a message unrelated to the cause.
todo_health_explanation: The things you believe are done and have never verified. None blocks anything — they are discovered at the worst moment.
health_no_destination: No destination declared: nothing is backed up anywhere.
health_single_destination: A single destination: one copy disappears with the machine carrying it, and a power failure takes both.
health_drill_never: Never rehearsed: nobody knows whether a restore works. The restore is the least-travelled path in the system, and the only one you discover on the worst day.
health_drill_due: Rehearsed {ago} ago — the aim is every {every}.
health_drill_overdue: Rehearsed {ago} ago. Past {late} the procedure has had time to drift: a path that moves, a password that rotates, a version that changes.
health_heartbeat_absent: No heartbeat: if everything stops, nothing will warn you.
health_heartbeat: Last heartbeat {ago} ago. This screen only attests to the heartbeat: the watchdog does not run here and cannot declare itself alive on its own.
health_admin_unknown: No admin token recorded: access may go through an OIDC session, which cannot be checked from here.
health_admin_single: A single admin token: that is the right number.
health_admin_tokens: {count} admin tokens in circulation: each one opens everything, and you no longer know which are still in use.
health_audit_intact: The chaining is intact: no entry was removed or modified.
health_audit_broken: The chaining is BROKEN: an entry was removed or modified.
health_audit_unreadable: The log could not be read back.
topology_anti_affinity_explanation: Anti-affinity must be about the HARDWARE, not the node: two virtual machines on the same server are two Swarm nodes and one point of failure.
topology_worst_case_at_top: Each row takes down a whole domain. The worst case is at the top.
topology_undeclared_domain_explanation: These nodes may share hardware — nothing lets us know. Declare it: hlb node add --failure-domain <name>
topology_concentrated_domain_explanation: This hardware carries more than half the cluster: losing it would take the quorum with it.
state_never_received: Nothing has been received: the request failed — {error}
state_stale: Controller unreachable — what follows is {age} old ({error})
state_gone: Nothing by that name here: it does not exist, or no longer does.
inbox_all_clear: Nothing needs you. Every source the inbox reads answered, and none has anything to report.
inbox_incomplete: The inbox could not be read — {error}. Something may need you.
palette_placeholder: Go to a page, an application, a machine…
action_previewing: Asking the controller what this would do…
action_blockers: Why it cannot be done as it stands

match.countPlural=one: Stopped: {count} step failed, and nothing after it was attempted.
match.countPlural=*: Stopped: {count} steps failed, and nothing after them was attempted.

match.countPlural=one: INCOMPLETE: {count} step cannot be performed by Homelabus yet — do it by hand.
match.countPlural=*: INCOMPLETE: {count} steps cannot be performed by Homelabus yet — do them by hand.

words_node_disk_full: {path} is {used} full: nothing more is deployed there
words_node_swapping: swapping: it slows down before it falls over
words_node_reboot_pending: waiting for a reboot to run its security fixes — hlb node upgrade does it, drained
words_coverage_never: NEVER backed up — it runs, and its data is protected by nothing

match.countPlural=one: no up-to-date copy: the only destination is too old
match.countPlural=*: no up-to-date copy: all {count} destinations are too old

match.countPlural=one: one up-to-date copy, out of {count} destination
match.countPlural=*: one up-to-date copy, out of {count} destinations

match.countPlural=one: {count} service has every replica on one piece of hardware
match.countPlural=*: {count} services have every replica on one piece of hardware

words_topology_concentrated: {nodes} of {total} machines on {domain}: losing it takes the quorum
words_topology_concentrated_unknown: {nodes} of {total} machines share an undeclared domain
words_topology_spread_unknown: some machines have no declared failure domain: the real spread is unknown
words_topology_no_machine: no machine known: nothing to judge the spread of
words_recovery_none_ever: no safeguard ever verified: if PocketID goes down, nothing says you can still get in
widget_exposure_none: Nothing is reachable from the internet.
app_diagnosis: Why it is in this state
app_unknown_cause: The search stopped before reaching a cause: that is "unknown", not "nothing".
app_scale_zero: Zero is not a size, it is a shutdown: remove the application instead.
need_database: {engine} database “{name}”, with a role of its own
need_database_extensions: {engine} database “{name}”, with a role of its own — the server's image must carry: {extensions}
need_sso_proxy_header: sign-in at the portal, which hands the identity over in a header
need_sso_proxy_only: the portal in front: the application has no accounts of its own
need_smtp: sending mail from an account of its own, which sends as itself only
need_smtp_person: sending mail as the person signed in, with their own mailbox
need_volume_sqlite: {need} (a SQLite database: copied from a snapshot)
rotation_step_change_in_postgres: Change the password IN PostgreSQL (ALTER ROLE … PASSWORD)
rotation_step_write_to_vault: Write the new value to the vault
rotation_step_redeploy_for_new_variable: Redeploy the app so it receives the new variable
rotation_step_regenerate_in_pocket_id: Regenerate the client secret IN PocketID
rotation_step_create_new_key_in_garage: Create a NEW key in Garage — the old one stays valid
rotation_step_write_to_vault_garage_neve: Write it to the vault: Garage will never show it again
rotation_step_delete_old_key_only_after_: Delete the old key ONLY after seeing the app work
rotation_step_redeploy_and_reconfigure_m: Redeploy the app, and reconfigure the mail clients
rotation_step_do_not_rotate_before_verif: Do NOT rotate before a restore has been verified
rotation_step_add_key_to_restic_reposito: Add the new key to the restic repository (restic key add)
rotation_step_remove_old_restic_key_afte: Remove the old key from the repository only after a successful drill
rotation_step_nothing_reads_it: Nothing reads it: Valkey runs without a password — it can be forgotten
rotation_step_create_new_key_at_s3_provi: Create a new key at the S3 provider
rotation_step_back_up_and_verify_it_succ: Run a backup and VERIFY it succeeds: a failed rotation only shows there
rotation_step_revoke_old_key_after_backu: Revoke the old key once that backup has passed
rotation_step_generate_new_key_at_provid: Generate a new key at the provider
rotation_step_reload_what_reads_it: Reload the configuration that reads it
rotation_consequence_redeploy_app: Requires redeploying {app}: without it, the app keeps the old value and fails without saying why.
rotation_consequence_redeploy_whatever: Requires redeploying whatever uses it: the application could not be derived from the name.
rotation_consequence_reload: Read on every use: reloading the configuration is enough.
alerts_muted_by: muted by {by} — {remaining} left; it stays visible, one notch lower
alerts_muted: muted — {remaining} left; it stays visible, one notch lower
audit_filter: Filter by person, action or target
people_role_user: user — their own mailbox and portal
people_role_admin: admin — everything, including destroying and granting
people_no_invitation: No invitation. An invitation is a link that lets someone create their own account.
people_widely_open: widely open — the one you forget to close
people_never_attested: never checked — we know nothing about it
settings_default_theme: Theme for everyone who chose none
settings_logo_explanation: PNG or SVG; an SVG is turned into an image on the server, since a logo is served to anyone and an SVG can carry script.
settings_exports_explanation: Every table you may want outside Homelabus — to keep, to print, to hand over.
me_alias_unknown: a state this version does not know
me_bitwarden_token: API key — shown this once only ({name})
uptime_private: This status page is private. Sign in to see it.
alerts_mute_reason_hint: what is being done about it
alerts_mute_explanation: It stops notifying, not showing: it stays here, one notch lower, until the mute ends.
settings_density_explanation: How tightly the lists are set: compact shows more rows on a screen. It follows you, like the theme.

alert_rule_backup_absent: Some applications have NO successful backup. They may be running perfectly — the worst state of the system, and the one that looks healthiest.
alert_rule_backup_late: A backup is more than 48 h old.
alert_rule_single_copy: An application has only ONE up-to-date copy left. The other destinations are configured but failing — configured is not protected.
alert_rule_verification_stale: No verified restore for over a month. A backup never restored is a hypothesis.
alert_rule_disk_full: A disk is over 85 %. Beyond that, backups and dumps have no room left to run.
alert_rule_blocking_guides: Manual steps are blocking an installation.
account_explain_complete: Identity and mailbox: the account is whole.
account_explain_without_mailbox: Identity created, NO mailbox: this person signs in everywhere and their address receives nothing. The first lost email will probably be a password reset. Running the creation again resumes where it stopped.
account_explain_without_identity: Mailbox created, NO identity: mail arrives and nobody can read it. Running the creation again finishes it.

roles_closed: closed — no role is let in
roles_sync_title: Make PocketID and the applications hold the roles
roles_explanation: A role is what someone may do here, which applications they enter and how much they may hold. Each one is a group in PocketID: an application lets in only the roles listed for it, and nobody when none is.

match.countPlural=one: {count} closed: an application no role is let into opens for nobody.
match.countPlural=*: {count} closed: an application no role is let into opens for nobody.

roles_no_app: No application signs anyone in through PocketID
roles_id_explanation: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It names the role's PocketID group and never changes.
accounts_quota_absent: waiting for their first sign-in to the application
invitations_choose_role: Choose the role the account will hold.
my_devices_explanation: A phone, a calendar or a mail app cannot sign in with a passkey. Give each device a password of its own: it opens your mail, calendars and contacts, and you revoke it alone when the device is lost, sold or replaced.
my_devices_unreadable: Your devices could not be read — {error}. A password may still be open.
device_setup_explanation: Shown once: nothing keeps a copy you could read again. Set the device up now — if you lose it before, revoke this one and make another.
device_setup_apple: iPhone, iPad or Mac: download the profile, open it on the device and install it from Settings. It holds the password — delete the file once it is installed.
device_setup_android: Android: in DAVx⁵, add an account with “Login with URL and user name”, the URL https://{server}, then the user name and password above.
device_setup_mail: Any mail app: IMAP on {server}, port 993, and SMTP on port 465, both with SSL/TLS and the same user name and password.
domain_explanation: The house's domain as the internet and its registry see it, read every night and compared with the reading accepted as its baseline: a registrar talked into moving the name servers is a theft no machine of the house sees.
domain_no_exposure: No domain yet: nothing is published by name, so nothing is watched.
domain_internal: {domain} is served under the house's own root: no registry holds it and no public authority certifies it, so there is nothing to watch.
domain_never_read: Not read yet: the controller reads the domain every night.
domain_stale: Not read for more than two days: what the last reading said still stands, but nothing is known since.
domain_baseline_at: Accepted {when}: every night is compared with that reading.
domain_baseline_none: No baseline accepted: nothing is compared, and a move would go unseen.
domain_accept_explanation: Accepting makes the reading taken now the baseline, and every certificate issued until now accepted — those found foreign included. Without --apply it only shows what would change.
domain_moved_explanation: If nobody here did this, call the registrar now.
domain_caa_unread: Which CAA governs was not read.
domain_caa_nothing: No CAA from the exposure's domain up to the zone: any authority may issue.
domain_no_account: No ACME account of the house read.
domain_verdict_any_account: allowed, as any account at its authority is
domain_verdict_refused: REFUSED by the CAA: its renewals will fail
domain_logs_unread: The watch's record could not be read: {why}
domain_logs_not_started: Not watched: no certificate is judged before a baseline is accepted.
domain_logs_clean: No certificate for the house's names under a key it does not hold.
domain_logs_foreign: Under a key the house does not hold: if nobody here asked for it, have its authority revoke it.
domain_advice_no_transfer_lock: No transfer lock: ask the registrar to set one, or a registry lock where offered.
domain_advice_expires: Expires in {days} days: a name that lapses is anyone's.
domain_advice_expired: Expired: a name that lapses is anyone's — renew it now.
domain_advice_not_signed: Not signed: no DS at the parent, so no DNSSEC.
domain_advice_signed_not_validating: Signed and not validating: a validating resolver refuses every name in it.
domain_advice_no_caa: No CAA: any certificate authority may issue for it.
domain_advice_pin_no_authority: No CAA names an authority, so any may issue for the house's names. These records at {at}, in place of its issue ones, let the house's accounts alone:
domain_advice_pin_no_account: The CAA names no account, so anyone's at the same authority may issue. These records at {at}, in place of its issue ones, let the house's accounts alone:
catalog_proven_explained: The catalog installs it on a fresh house, updates it from the published version, backs it up, restores it and removes it. The result is signed with the index.

match.countPlural=one: An update of {shown} application waits for your approval
match.countPlural=*: Updates of {shown} applications wait for your approval

match.countPlural=one: A major update of {shown} application is applied by hand
match.countPlural=*: Major updates of {shown} applications are applied by hand

match.countPlural=one: An update of {shown} application was refused while nobody was there
match.countPlural=*: Updates of {shown} applications were refused while nobody was there

reason_update_needs_approval: an update waits for your approval
reason_update_needs_hands: a major update, applied by hand: hlb update apply
reason_update_refused: its update was refused while nobody was there
updates_intro: Patches apply themselves in each application's maintenance window, after a backup. A minor update waits for your approval once you have read its notes; the same pass then applies it in its window. A major one is applied by hand, with its migration guide.
updates_none: No update waits: every application runs what its channel offers.
updates_why_major: a major update: its migration guide first
updates_why_beyond_house: a {jump} update, and the house applies {reach} alone
updates_why_beyond_manifest: a {jump} update, and its manifest applies {reach} alone
updates_why_notes_say: the notes of {tag} say “{word}”: read them first
updates_why_notes_missing: no release notes found for {tag}: nobody read what it changes
updates_why_notes_unreadable: its release notes could not be read
updates_refused_vulnerable: Its scan refused it: nothing switched.
updates_refused_copy_failed: The backup owed first failed: nothing switched.
updates_refused_rolled_back: Swarm rolled it back: the previous version runs.
updates_refused_paused: The switch paused: look at it before anything else.
updates_refused_inconclusive: No outcome within the time allotted: check with hlb ps.
